body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE TEXT for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in exactly the format asked at the end.

"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG (think Baldur's Gate 3: fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). It is folk horror set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face; drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the stakes are real. Humour is deadpan and sits beside the dread.

THIS SCENE: Chapter 20, "The Roving Rookery". The village of Wickermoor has been swept into a mass hysteria by Golub Graygullet, a pigeon hag who has lived seventy years among the villagers wearing other women's skins, lately as the postmaster Theodora Mayville. She staged a murder, pinned it on the party (four level 10 heroes) with a forged letter, and charmed the whole village: every neighbour is hostile, doors are barred, shops shut, mobs with torches walk the lanes, and grey pigeons line every roof. A tell of the charm is a lilac glint in the eyes. Her flying, walking dovecote stands up on pigeon legs and roams between four roosts. Peeping Albert is her spy: a pudgy pigeon with a wrinkled bald human head, human ears, and hands for talons; he is terrified of dogs. Cast: Constable Doris Squire (tall, stocky, laconic, writes poetry in secret), Deputy Howie Butterman (friendly, false, a hidden cultist), Mayor Wendel Somerton (officious, loves forms, bowler hat, waxed moustache), Tamsin Ledger (deadpan auditor, treats strangeness as a clerical error), Ambrose Quill (grand hopeless poet), Sergeant Gaunt (overconfident coward), Pip Oakum (a small boy who trades buttons), Mrs. Oakum (hill-country twang, a werewolf who only wants to hurt no one), Marianna Grey (shy stablemistress), Weston Murdoch (warm Brightsinger preacher), Hilda Brom (terse huntress), Geneva Fairchild (earnest assistant, lilac eyes), Phillip and Adela Druskenvald (dapper theatrical lord; bright slangy lady), Dani Jenkin (child with a hound called Shuck), Jeremiah Stover (stubborn tuber farmer).

RULES FOR THE TEXT
- Spoken lines: 1 to 3 short sentences, about 12 to 30 words, never over 45. Contractions are normal. People talk in their own voice and do not explain the plot to the audience. Accent is word choice and rhythm, never phonetic spelling.
- Option lines (what the player's party says or does): under 12 words, plain, in the party's voice ("We..." or an imperative).
- Narrator lines ("The Vagrant", a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, never gloating): second person, present tense, one or two sentences, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never the word "suddenly". Never mention the Vagrant by name inside the line.
- No stage directions, asterisks, italics, brackets, placeholders, emoji or em dashes (use commas, periods, colons). Straight quotes only. Do not use the arrow characters -> or => inside the text.
- Content is dark but restrained: no gore, no graphic detail.
- Each brief inside <<...>> says what the line must do; keep its facts, write it as the speaker would say it. Where it says "The Vagrant:" it is a Narrator line.

## The conversation file `posse` (structure is fixed; only the [[n]] markers are yours)

```
# R20: the posse at the post office door. Doris holds a forged letter; they are charmed. Talk, run, give up or fight.

~ start
Narrator: [[1]]
doris_squire [angry]: [[2]]
-> menu

~ menu
* [Insight DC 18] [[3]] -> charm | charm_missed
* [if flag.rk_charm_seen] [Persuasion DC 18] [[4]] -> talk_down | talk_fail
* [if flag.rk_charm_seen] [Deception DC 18] [[5]] -> talk_down | talk_fail
* [Intimidation DC 20] [[6]] -> talk_down | talk_fail
* [knows:dispel_magic] [[7]] -> spell
* [knows:remove_curse] [[8]] -> spell
* [[9]] -> flee
* [[10]] -> surrender
* [[11]] -> fight

~ charm
set rk_charm_seen
Narrator: [[12]]
-> menu
~ charm_missed
Narrator: [[13]]
-> menu

~ talk_fail
doris_squire [angry]: [[14]]
-> menu_after_fail

~ menu_after_fail
* [knows:dispel_magic] [[15]] -> spell
* [knows:remove_curse] [[16]] -> spell
* [[17]] -> flee
* [[18]] -> surrender
* [[19]] -> fight

~ talk_down
set posse_outcome = "talked"
set rk_posse_done
quest roving_rookery hysteria
doris_squire [weary]: [[20]]
Narrator: [[21]]
-> END

~ spell
set posse_outcome = "talked"
set rk_posse_done
set doris_cleared
quest roving_rookery hysteria
Narrator: [[22]]
doris_squire [neutral]: [[23]]
-> END

~ flee
set posse_outcome = "fled"
set rk_posse_done
quest roving_rookery hysteria
Narrator: [[24]]
move wickermoor_village:from_estate

~ fight
set posse_outcome = "fought"
Narrator: [[25]]
combat rk_posse

~ surrender
set posse_outcome = "surrendered"
set rk_posse_done
set jail_began = now
quest roving_rookery jailed
doris_squire [neutral]: [[26]]
Narrator: [[27]]
jail wickermoor_constable_station:cells until flag.jail_free

~ howie
howie_butterman [smile]: [[28]]
-> start

~ grunt
Narrator: [[29]]
-> END
```

## Briefs

1. node `start`, narrator: The Vagrant: the posse fills the lane, torches and cudgels, Doris Squire in front with a letter held up like a warrant
2. node `start`, spoken by doris_squire: Doris, clipped, says the letter names you as the postmaster's killers; hands up, quietly, or she takes you by force; she says very few words
3. node `menu`, option: Look closely at Doris's eyes and the faces behind her.
4. node `menu`, option: Tell Doris the letter is a forgery and she is not herself.
5. node `menu`, option: Swear we found the body that way and send the posse after Geneva.
6. node `menu`, option: Warn her what the posse will cost her if it comes closer.
7. node `menu`, option: Cast Dispel Magic on Doris.
8. node `menu`, option: Cast Remove Curse on Doris.
9. node `menu`, option: Run: the east alley behind the post office.
10. node `menu`, option: Put our hands up and go with them.
11. node `menu`, option: Fight our way out.
12. node `charm`, narrator: The Vagrant: a lilac glint in every eye, steady and unblinking; the posse is not angry, it is being walked
13. node `charm_missed`, narrator: The Vagrant: all you see is an angry mob with the sort of faces that came straight from supper
14. node `talk_fail`, spoken by doris_squire: Doris says no, and signals the deputies forward; two words and a step
15. node `menu_after_fail`, option: Cast Dispel Magic on Doris.
16. node `menu_after_fail`, option: Cast Remove Curse on Doris.
17. node `menu_after_fail`, option: Run: the east alley behind the post office.
18. node `menu_after_fail`, option: Put our hands up and go with them.
19. node `menu_after_fail`, option: Fight our way out.
20. node `talk_down`, spoken by doris_squire: Doris wavers, frowns at the letter, and says she gives you an hour, no more; she has seen the pigeons too
21. node `talk_down`, narrator: The Vagrant: the posse goes slowly back toward the Round, still chanting; the hysteria has not lifted, only paused
22. node `spell`, narrator: The Vagrant: the magic runs over her like cold water and the lilac glint goes out of her eyes; for an hour Doris Squire is herself
23. node `spell`, spoken by doris_squire: Doris sniffs the letter, mutters that the ink stinks of pigeon, and tells you to go, quickly, before the charm creeps back
24. node `flee`, narrator: The Vagrant: you bolt down the east alley, over a fence, and through someone's cabbages; the shouting follows you all the way to the estate road
25. node `fight`, narrator: The Vagrant: Doris sets her feet and the deputies come on
26. node `surrender`, spoken by doris_squire: Doris, grimly, says gear off, hands where she can see them; a bed and a bucket until the Witching Hour
27. node `surrender`, narrator: The Vagrant: the cell door is only a barred frame, but there is nowhere in Wickermoor to take what they have kept; across the Round the mob is already chanting
28. node `howie`, spoken by howie_butterman: Howie, friendly and false, says it would all go easier if you come along quietly; he can speak to Doris about a quick trial
29. node `grunt`, narrator: The Vagrant: a deputy in an armband stares through you and mutters your names in rhythm, over and over

## Reply format
One line per marker, in order, exactly `n => text` (no quotes around the text, no extra lines, no commentary). 29 lines.

1 => Torches and heavy cudgels crowd the narrow lane, smelling of pitch and sour wool. Doris Squire stands in front, holding up a folded letter like a warrant.
2 => This letter names you the postmaster's killers. Hands up, come along quiet, or we take you down by force.
3 => Study Doris's eyes and the faces crowded behind her.
4 => Tell Doris the letter is forged and her mind isn't her own.
5 => Swear we found the body and blame Geneva instead.
6 => Warn her what this mob will cost her if they step closer.
7 => Cast Dispel Magic on Doris.
8 => Cast Remove Curse on Doris.
9 => Bolt down the east alley behind the post office.
10 => Put our hands up and go with them quietly.
11 => Draw weapons and fight our way through.
12 => A flat lilac glint sits in every single eye, steady and unblinking in the torchlight. This posse isn't angry, friends: it's being walked on a leash.
13 => All you can make out in the smoky glare is a press of grim, tight-jawed faces that came straight from the supper table.
14 => No. Take them.
15 => Cast Dispel Magic on Doris.
16 => Cast Remove Curse on Doris.
17 => Bolt down the east alley behind the post office.
18 => Put our hands up and go with them quietly.
19 => Draw weapons and fight our way through.
20 => Wait a minute, this hand isn't right. I've seen those grey birds watching the roofs too, so you get one hour, no more.
21 => The crowd shuffles slowly back toward the Round, their boots scraping the cobbles as they keep up a low chant. The fever hasn't broken, only paused.
22 => The spell runs over her like a bucket of well water, and the lilac shine drains right out of her eyes. For the next hour, Doris Squire is her own woman.
23 => Bah, this ink reeks of wet pigeon feathers. Get moving, quick now, before that purple fog creeps back into my head.
24 => You bolt down the dark alley, vault a splintered rail, and tear straight through somebody's winter cabbages. Their hoarse shouting chases your heels all the way to the estate road.
25 => Doris plants her heavy boots on the stones, and the deputies surge forward with their clubs raised.
26 => Gear on the stones, hands where I can see them. You get a cot and a bucket until the Witching Hour.
27 => The cell door is little more than an iron frame, though there's nowhere in Wickermoor left to run. Across the Round, you can already hear the mob chanting in the dark.
28 => It'll go a whole lot easier on everyone if you just walk along quiet-like, friends. I can put a warm word in Doris's ear for a quick trial.
29 => A deputy in a linen armband stares straight through your shoulder, muttering your names under his breath in a slow, steady rhythm.
